title: Dynamics and stabilization of topological edge solitons in driven-damped nonlinear SSH lattices
authors: Adrianus Yosia, Rahmi Rusin, Rudy Kusdiantara, Hadi Susanto
abstract: We study topological edge solitons in a nonlinear Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) lattice subject to parametric driving and linear damping. Starting from a vertically driven pendulum chain, we derive an effective driven--damped nonlinear SSH model and investigate its stationary edge-localized states. Analytical calculations reveal the existence of two phase-locked dissipative edge-soliton families that emerge from the nonlinear continuation of the topological edge mode. Using numerical continuation and spectral stability analysis, we construct the corresponding nonlinear branches and determine their stability properties. We show that parametric driving and damping fundamentally modify the conservative edge-state family by generating two dissipative branches with markedly different stability characteristics: one branch remains predominantly unstable, whereas the other develops substantially larger stability regions and significantly weaker instability growth rates. Direct numerical simulations further demonstrate that the robust branch can remain strongly localized over long time intervals even when weakly unstable. Simulations of the full driven--damped Klein--Gordon pendulum chain confirm the persistence of the edge-localized dynamics predicted by the reduced model. These results identify parametric driving and damping as an effective mechanism for enhancing the robustness and persistence of nonlinear topological localization in active lattice systems.
summary: The paper analyzes how parametric driving and damping stabilize topological edge solitons in a nonlinear SSH lattice model. By deriving an effective amplitude equation, the authors show that these external forces create two distinct soliton branches with vastly different stabilities. This demonstrates that active control mechanisms can enhance the robustness of quantum-like localization phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamics and stabilization of topological edge solitons within a nonlinear Su–Schrieffer–Heeger (SSH) lattice that is subjected to both parametric driving and linear damping.
main_result: Parametric driving and damping fundamentally modify the system's edge-state family, generating two dissipative branches; one branch can exhibit significantly enhanced stability compared to the conservative case.
method: The research employs analytical derivations from a driven pendulum chain, followed by numerical continuation and spectral stability analysis on an effective reduced SSH amplitude model.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a 1D lattice of pendula (analogous to SSH) governed by equations derived from a Klein-Gordon equation. The final effective model is a driven-damped discrete nonlinear Schrödinger type equation.
key_observables: Topological edge solitons, total power ($P$), and the real parts of linearization eigenvalues ($	ext{Re}(\lambda)$) used to determine stability.
important_parameters: Damping ($\Gamma$), parametric drive strength ($h$), detuning parameter ($\Delta$), and coupling constants ($c_{n}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes weak damping, small-amplitude oscillations, and utilizes an exponentially decaying spatial profile ansatz for the edge state approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate experimental setups (pendulum chain), bifurcation diagrams showing total power vs. detuning, stationary edge-state profiles under different driving conditions, and time evolution comparisons between the reduced model and the full lattice dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving an effective driven-damped SSH model from a physical pendulum chain to performing analytical calculations for phase-locked states, followed by detailed numerical stability analysis and comparison with direct time-domain simulations.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete theoretical tools (stability analysis of dissipative nonlinear systems) applicable to understanding robust localized excitations in active or driven quantum/classical lattices, which is highly relevant to open quantum system dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Sketch of a possible experimental setup for a parametrically driven pendulum chain. Identical pendula are coupled via torsional springs mounted on a common support that oscillates vertically with a prescribed harmonic motion, thereby providing parametric excitation. Alternating coupling stiffnesses (indicated by varying spring lengths) emulate the dimerized Su–Schrieffer–Heeger (SSH) configuration.

FIG. 4: Representative stationary edge states and their linearization spectra for ω = 0.37 and c2 = 1. Each group of panels shows Re(An), Im(An), and the corresponding spectrum of the linearized operator. The parameters are (a) Γ = 0, h = 0, c1 = 0.6, (b) Γ = 0.04, h = 0.05, c1 = 0.6, and (c) Γ = 0.04, h = −0.05, c1 = 0.6. The selected solutions are spectrally unstable. Panels (a) and (c) exhibit oscillatory instabilities associated with complex unstable eigenvalues, whereas panel (b) exhibits an exponential instability associated with a real positive eigenvalue.

FIG. 5: Maximum real part of the linearization eigenvalues, max Re(λ), in the (ω, c1)-parameter plane. The three panels correspond to (a) Γ = 0, h = 0, (b) Γ = 0.04, h = 0.05, and (c) Γ = 0.04, h = −0.05. Values at or below zero, up to numerical tolerance, correspond to spectrally stable stationary edge states, whereas positive values indicate instability. The dashed curve marks the boundary of the edge-localized existence region predicted by the analytical approximation.
